critical.name: Legacy seeded exclusions file never gains the scratch row
critical.summary: ensure_default_exclusions never overwrites an existing file, and both pattern loaders read only that file. A project seeded by PR 45 keeps its 5-row list, so every pr-review capture writes untracked scratch files and build's Phase 4 first run STOPs after the full reviewer fan-out. The only remedy is a hand edit (reproduced by the adversarial reviewer: 'STOP ... ?? docs/_scratch/pr_review/0072/current'; code trace: _exclusion_patterns loads only the named file, review_plan.exclusion_patterns likewise).
fix: Union default_patterns(cfg) into the loaded patterns in memory whenever cfg.exclusions is non-null: in _exclusion_patterns (phase4_branch_safety.py) and in review_plan.exclusion_patterns. Write nothing, so the file stays the user's list and harness artifact folders are always exempt. Skip the union when --exclusions-fixture overrides the file, so fixture runs stay hermetic. Add a legacy-file test: a project whose file lists only five old rows still passes _check_clean_tree with an untracked scratch file.

important.name: Seeded rows miss state_dir and commit_messages and skip path normalization
important.summary: Three gaps in default_exclusions._entries, all reproduced by the adversarial reviewer. (1) Untracked files under state_dir (default .claude/state/harness/: stale or other-session phase5 sentinels, pr-team runtime outputs, pr-sum and parallel2 state, todo-sync runner.json) STOP Phase 4 in the main checkout; there is no state_dir row. (2) docs/_commit_messages/*.txt drafts from c-msg and branch-commit-msg are untracked in a project that does not gitignore them and STOP Phase 4; there is no artifacts.commit_messages row. The drafts are harness output, so hiding them from review capture is harmless. (3) The reviews, summaries and scratch rows use only rstrip('/'), while the rows-file entries go through _normalized: scratch './tmp/runs' yields './tmp/runs/*', which never matches the porcelain path 'tmp/runs/x'.
fix: In _entries of default_exclusions.py do all three together: add the rows (f"{_normalized(cfg.state_dir)}/*", "harness runtime state") and (f"{_normalized(cfg.artifacts.commit_messages)}/*", "commit message drafts"), and build the reviews, summaries and scratch folder rows with f"{_normalized(x)}/*". Add tests in tests/lib/test_default_exclusions.py that default_patterns holds both new rows, follows a configured state_dir and commit_messages, and normalizes a './'-prefixed scratch value.

important.name: build STOP line names neither the dirty paths nor the remedy
important.summary: A failed Phase 4 first run prints only 'phase4 first run rc 1: a branch-safety check failed; pre_fix_time left pending (see <run>/phase4_first_run.json); STOP'. The user must open the JSON to find 'STOP: working tree has non-exempt changes' and gets no hint about the exclusions file or the pattern to add (_phase4_reason returns a generic string at pr_review.py:1322-1328).
fix: Make _phase4_reason name the failed checks and, for clean_tree_check, the filtered_stdout paths and the configured exclusions file. Keep the one-line problem format; cap the path list.

important.name: Check 3 shell snippet omits --untracked-files=all
important.summary: The documented shell form of the clean-tree check runs plain 'git status --porcelain'. When docs/_scratch/ is wholly untracked, git prints one '?? docs/_scratch/' line that the pattern 'docs/_scratch/pr_review/*' never matches, so an agent following the snippet gets a false STOP. The script (phase4_branch_safety.py _STATUS_ARGS) is correct. Predates this PR, but the new row depends on it.
fix: Add --untracked-files=all to both git status lines of the Check 3 snippet in SKILL.md.

minor.name: Broad scratch folder swallows its subtree
minor.summary: fnmatch '*' crosses '/', so artifacts.scratch set to a broad folder such as 'docs' seeds 'docs/*' and hides every docs change from Phase 4 and from review capture. Reproduced by the adversarial reviewer. The same footgun exists for reviews and summaries.
fix: Add one sentence to the README exclusions row: the folder rows cover the whole subtree, so point artifacts.scratch, reviews and summaries at dedicated folders.

minor.name: Stale 'project keeps git-ignored' wording
minor.summary: SKILL.md says the run directory is one 'which the project keeps git-ignored', and pr_review.py repeats it. The seeded scratch row makes the gitignore unnecessary, and the wording implies a hand step.
fix: Reword both: the run directory is machine-generated and exempt through the seeded exclusions file.

minor.name: No end-to-end test of the original failure
minor.summary: tests/lib/test_default_exclusions.py only asserts list membership and plain fnmatch. Nothing runs an untracked scratch file through _check_clean_tree, and nothing covers a legacy five-row file, which is the real failure.
fix: In test_phase4_branch_safety_second_run.py add an untracked docs/_scratch/pr_review/0001/current file to the default-exclusions clean-tree test, and add a legacy-file test that fails before the C1 fix.

minor.name: Gitignore test contradicts the commit/PR claim and guards nothing
minor.summary:
The commit title and body say the seed gains a snapshot of the plain root .gitignore lines. default_exclusions.py:28-40 (_entries) has no .gitignore reading, and the README row documents only the scratch row. test_gitignore_lines_are_not_snapshotted asserts the opposite of the commit message (lines absent). The test therefore passes trivially against code that never reads .gitignore: it exercises no new logic and cannot fail until someone implements the feature the commit describes, at which point it fails by design. Either the PR omits the described behavior or the test and PR text disagree on intent.

Also (overall): The head commit 1aa9d79 and the PR title/body say the seed writes 'a snapshot of the plain root .gitignore lines (folder lines at any depth unless anchored; comments, negations and ** lines skipped)'. Nothing in default_exclusions.py reads .gitignore: _entries (lines 28-40) adds only the scratch row, and the new test test_gitignore_lines_are_not_snapshotted (test file lines 72-77) asserts the opposite of the description, that build/* and *.pyc are NOT seeded. The README row and the module docstring agree with the code, so only the history is wrong, but a reader of the merged result who goes by the log will believe gitignored folders are filtered by the seeded file.
fix: If the snapshot is intended: implement it in _entries and replace this test with positive assertions (folder line 'build/' seeded as 'build/*' and '*/build/*' or equivalent, comments, negations and ** lines skipped)
If it is not intended: delete test_gitignore_lines_are_not_snapshotted and reword the PR title and commit body to cover only the scratch row

Reword the PR title, PR body and squash-merge commit message to drop the .gitignore clause (e.g. 'fix(harness): seed the run scratch folder into review exclusions') and say the new test pins that .gitignore lines are deliberately not copied.

Or implement the described .gitignore snapshot in _entries, update the README exclusions row, and replace test_gitignore_lines_are_not_snapshotted with tests for the anchored/unanchored, comment, negation and ** cases.

bubble_up.reason: Code is as the developer decided (snapshot dropped; test pins that). Only the PR title and commit 1aa9d79 text still mention the snapshot; the developer rewords them.
